violated_contract: A schema field whose pydantic default doubles as the internal 'no value arrived' sentinel must never be persisted as row content through a path that never received the field. Once stored, a defaulted value is indistinguishable from one the model or a rule chose, so the user is shown a deliberate-looking value that no code actually decided — 🧠 served as a chosen brain badge on every conversation whose writer simply forgot the emoji field. The trap is that the sentinel is repaired at one boundary and siblings keep leaking it: #23389 fixed the v2 NotesOutput conversion, while the sync-intake deterministic minimum, the short-clip and media minimums, the legacy StructuredExtraction/AgentNotesSubmission writers, the share and client-projection defaults, and the app's own decode fallback all still persisted or rendered the sentinel.
canonical_prevention: Repair the sentinel at the shared conversion boundary (fallback at to_structured), make the stored model's own default the neutral value so a forgotten field cannot land on the sentinel, have every deterministic builder set the category fallback explicitly, and make each client decode fallback use the same neutral value. The guard is a behavioral test that enumerates every deterministic/minimum builder and every no-LLM default and asserts none persists the sentinel.
